reason: The lawn is projected to need at least a normal 5.0 mm watering within the next 2 days.

duration.efficiency_note: Recommended depth is a gross application: the crop demand is divided by the irrigation efficiency before the run time is calculated.

freshness.note: Fetched from Open-Meteo for this request. GreenFlow does not cache weather results, so this recommendation uses live data.

sources.label: Kc
sources.citation: FAO-56 Table 12, p. 112: cool-season turfgrass Kc mid 0.95; warm-season turfgrass Kc mid 0.85 (footnote 15).

sources.label: Depletion fraction
sources.citation: FAO-56 Table 22, p. 165: turfgrass depletion fraction p = 0.40 (cool season) and p = 0.50 (warm season).

sources.label: Soil water
sources.citation: FAO-56 Table 19, p. 144: field capacity and wilting point ranges; midpoints are used for each supported soil texture.

sources.label: Root depth
sources.citation: Penn State Extension, The Cool-Season Turfgrasses: rooting depth is usually between 2 and 6 inches

sources.label: Irrigation efficiency
sources.citation: Colorado State University Extension, Drip Irrigation for Home Gardens: sprinkler systems are 50 to 70 percent efficient

sources.label: Weather and ET₀
sources.citation: Open-Meteo forecast API: precipitation_sum and et0_fao_evapotranspiration (FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration).

factors.label: Forecast reference ET₀
factors.detail: Summed over the 2-day decision horizon and converted to crop demand with the grass coefficient.

factors.label: Forecast rainfall
factors.detail: Rain in the decision horizon is credited against soil-water depletion.

factors.label: Rain since last watering
factors.detail: Observed daily rainfall since the last watering date you recorded.

factors.label: Depletion after last watering
factors.detail: clamp(RAW − applied depth, 0, TAW) with the assumption that the root zone was at the refill point before that watering.

factors.label: Soil water capacity
factors.detail: clay soil: field capacity 0.36 and wilting point 0.22 m³/m³ over a 0.15 m root zone.

factors.label: Skip threshold
factors.detail: 50% of RAW, a product policy. A projected depletion at or below this value produces a SKIP recommendation.

factors.label: Irrigation efficiency
factors.detail: Cited default used to convert crop demand into a gross applied depth before run time is calculated.

factors.label: Grass type
factors.detail: Crop coefficient 0.85 and depletion fraction 0.50 selected for this grass.

factors.label: Sprinkler precipitation rate
factors.detail: Used with the recommended depth to calculate run time in minutes.

factors.label: Lawn area
factors.detail: Used for water-volume estimates on the savings screen, not for the depth decision.

factors.label: Location
factors.detail: Weather is requested for the saved latitude and longitude.

uncertainty: Based on a 2-day weather forecast that can change. Check local conditions before watering.
limitations: ET₀ is Open-Meteo's FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration, not a reading from a weather station in your yard.
The water balance assumes the root zone was at the refill point before the last watering you recorded.
Rainfall is a gridded weather value and may differ from the rain that reached your lawn.
Irrigation efficiency is a cited 60% default; it is not a catch-cup measurement of your sprinkler system.
Weather forecasts can change after this recommendation is created.
GreenFlow does not measure soil moisture, water flow, or actual water use.
GreenFlow provides advice only; it does not control or modify your irrigation timer.
assumptions: Baseline schedule: 5 event(s) per week at 5.0 mm per event.
Decision horizon: 2 day(s) until the next scheduled watering.
No irrigation is assumed on forecast days.
The root zone was at the refill point before the last watering.
Weather data is from Open-Meteo and may change.
FAO-56 Table 12, p. 112 (turfgrass rows), warm-season turfgrass Kc mid=0.85; FAO-56 Table 22, p. 165 (turfgrass rows), warm-season turfgrass p=0.50.
FAO-56 Table 19, p. 144, Clay: FC 0.32-0.40, WP 0.20-0.24 m3/m3; midpoints 0.36 and 0.22 used.
Penn State Extension, The Cool-Season Turfgrasses: rooting depth is usually between 2 and 6 inches; the 6-inch upper bound (0.15 m) is used.

Colorado State University Extension, Drip Irrigation for Home Gardens: sprinkler systems are 50 to 70 percent efficient; the 60 percent midpoint is used as a default because no catch-cup measurement exists.
Skip threshold 50% of RAW and a 7-day horizon cap are product policies.
